name: Intrinsic Dimensionality (Topological Complexity)
description: Estimates the Intrinsic Dimension (ID) of the text's semantic embedding space. AI-generated texts typically occupy a lower-dimensional manifold (a simpler, flatter topological shape) compared to the highly complex, multi-dimensional structures of human text.
algorithm: Maximum Likelihood Estimation of Embedding Manifold Dimensionality
mechanism: When text is converted into high-dimensional vector embeddings, the actual 'shape' of the data does not occupy the entire mathematical space; it lies on a lower-dimensional manifold. The 'Intrinsic Dimension' (ID) measures the true number of independent variables needed to accurately describe this shape. Because Large Language Models (LLMs) are essentially extreme data compression engines that optimize for highly probable, smoothed sequences, the text they generate naturally collapses into a much simpler topological structure. Human cognition, however, produces text with abrupt conceptual jumps, chaotic associative links, and unique lexical combinations, resulting in a highly complex, higher-dimensional manifold. This algorithm extracts hidden-state embeddings from the text using a reference transformer model and applies Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) based on the distances between neighboring embedding vectors. If the estimated Intrinsic Dimension forms an unnaturally tight, low-complexity cluster, it mathematically proves the text was generated by a probability-optimized neural network rather than a human brain.
useCase: Highly advanced structural analysis for academic papers, legal documents, and literary works where standard lexical metrics fail but the underlying semantic topology reveals artificial generation.
strengths:
• Represents one of the most mathematically rigorous and robust methods available for AI detection, as it analyzes the fundamental topological limits of neural network outputs.
• Extremely difficult for humans or adversarial prompt engineers to defeat; bypassing it requires completely fundamentally altering the statistical shape of the embedding space, which cannot be done simply by swapping synonyms or forcing typos.
• Operates entirely independent of language syntax or specific vocabulary.
limitations:
• Computationally highly expensive. It requires running the text through a secondary transformer model to extract embeddings before dimension estimation can even begin.
• Requires a longer text sample (typically 200+ words) to generate enough embedding vectors to form a measurable manifold; completely ineffective on short sentences.
• Results can vary slightly depending on the specific base model used to generate the reference embeddings.
parameters:
Analysis: Point-Cloud Distance Mapping & Maximum Likelihood Estimation
Metric: Estimated Number of Local Degrees of Freedom (Intrinsic Dimension)
Output: 0-100 Topological Simplicity (Dimensional Collapse) Score
accuracy: Exceptional — 85-92% on sufficient text lengths. It provides a near-unfakeable mathematical signature of autoregressive text generation.

references.title: Tulchinskii, E. et al. (2023). Intrinsic Dimension Estimation for Robust Detection of AI-Generated Texts. NeurIPS.
Mitchell, E. et al. (2023). DetectGPT: Zero-Shot Machine-Generated Text Detection using Probability Curvature. ICML.
